page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 31 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, it allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The CPU features a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). This instance includes 137 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and does not bundle any GPU resources or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a mix of single-core strength and multi-core constraints. Single-threaded performance is notable, with gzip compression registering a strong 35.55 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing reaching top-tier levels at 2828.0. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weaker. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test scored 4549.86, and the large-block uncached read memory bandwidth was poor at 22.46 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are average, processing prompts at 591.08 tokens/sec, but drop significantly to a poor 5.04 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-4-lssd provides a high ratio of memory to vCPUs alongside fast local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for workloads that require moderate compute but benefit from larger memory footprints and low-latency local storage. However, the weak multi-core scaling and limited memory bandwidth represent clear tradeoffs for highly parallelized or memory-intensive processing. This instance is best suited for single-threaded tasks, lightweight database operations, text processing, and memory-bound applications that do not require massive parallel computing power.
